searchText: Is the crLists size always at max full block? As the block builder would need to include the whole list. crList's size is arbitrary, the builder needs to include it or prove that he ran out of space in the block. So if the builder has a full block already, he may not include any of the crList ah, so the builder could include some txt's from the crList and then the crList needs to be updated for the next block CL call in 25 minutes! CL call now what happens in Danksharding if the data is actually lost. Is there a way to recover the chain or does the whole chain get wrecked? Quick call notes: https://hackmd.io/@benjaminion/r1nwpZHe9 sharding relies on being able to *not follow* unavailable chains note though, that data availability does not guarantee (nor care about) perpetual data persistence. so there is a not a guarantee that data will be available forever but instead taht those that want the data *can* get it when following the tip and then manage it how they please Is that so? I thought the guarantee of sharding is that those that follow the tip *are guaranteed* that the data is available, but there is no enforcement in place to force peers to actually serve it, is there? those that want it need to be able to get it. in the worst case, there is *only* sampling. thus data can be retrieved via the sampling mechanism itself (and then reconstructed) sharding assumes DAS works if DAS works, then the data can be retrieved for recent blocks the whole point of DA is to be able to prevent data-withholding attacks which means that the data is in fact availble on the network (in some form) (for some amount of time) Understood, but still it's a way of actually attacking the UX of the network without penalties. Just withhold all data unless asked for DAS. Users would be to be sophisticated enough to restore the data they're interested from the samplings IIUC, data availability sampling enforces (at the protocol layer) that all of the data was sampled (provably) by some portion of attestors. So we can assert that at time of block attestation at least, the data for the block was available and downloaded by `n` validators. Whether those validators are willing to share it is a separate problem, and we want `n` sufficiently high so it is very unlikely that `0 of n` make the data available to the wider network. Also nodes sample as well. Not just vals And vals will likely be enforced to *custody" a larger amount of data than is required by a node to sample Which allows for reconstruction of missing data in emergencies Proof of custody (vals) and das (all nodes) complement eachother There is nothing that forces a validator to respond to individual nodes that are sampling though, right? No reward for responding, nor punishment for ignoring. Right, my understanding is that the validator holding the data can and is forced to prove that it has it, but is not required to produce it. At least I have not seen any design that punishes validators that do not serve the actual data Also because that's hard: how do you prove that you requested data and your didn't get it?
